卡姆布斯琴見於葉門與阿曼傳統音樂，也隨葉門移民傳入印度洋沿岸；在印尼、馬來西亞、: The qanbus appears in the traditional music of Yemen and Oman, and travelled with Yemeni emigrants to the Indian Ocean coast; among Muslim communities in Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei it is used for the zapin dance, Malay ghazal and gambus ensembles. In Kenya and Tanzania in East Africa there is a related instrument, the kibangala, and in the Comoros and Zanzibar the gabusi or gambusi.
卡姆布斯琴起源於葉門，傳遍阿拉伯半島，與中亞可能蒙皮的巴爾巴特琴相關；薩克斯認為: The qanbus originated in Yemen and spread through the Arabian peninsula; it is probably related to the Central Asian barbat, which may have had a skin soundboard, and Sachs held that its name comes from the Turkic komuz. Its popularity declined under the Imam Yahya in the early twentieth century, and in the early twenty-first the oud replaced it as the first choice of Middle Eastern lute players. Yemeni emigrants carried it into the Indian Ocean, and related instruments appeared in the Comoros, Zanzibar, Kenya and Tanzania. In the Muslim world of Southeast Asia it is called the gambus, thought to have arrived between the ninth and fifteenth centuries; the Malay type and the Hadhrami type probably arrived at different times, the latter developing alongside the oud in the nineteenth century and giving rise to the zapin dance, Malay ghazal and the gambus ensemble.
卡姆布斯琴音色明亮而富有穿透力，具有獨特的金屬質感與溫暖的共鳴特徵。其6至7根尼: The qanbus has a bright, carrying timbre, with a distinctive metallic quality and a warm resonance. Its six or seven nylon strings, plucked with a plectrum, give a clear, grainy sound; the range covers the middle and upper register, the volume is moderate but expressive. Because there are no frets, the strings drive the body directly, which makes the resonance more natural and full, and the timbre falls between the warmth of the oud and the brightness of the modern guitar. It has both the character of the traditional Arab lute family and a desert flavour of its own: brighter than the oud, more Eastern in colour than the guitar, and able to shape delicate ornaments and slides.
